content: To date, the implementation of the One Health approach has involved summarizing progress, milestones, and lessons learned from national efforts. This includes detailing existing mechanisms, strategies, plans, frameworks, and activities, which are further analyzed in the situation analysis section. Templates for developing a national One Health action plan and an associated workplan are available for download, as provided by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2023. The purpose of the national One Health action plan is to either strengthen an existing plan or develop a new one that aligns with the One Health Joint Plan of Action (OH JPA). This plan integrates and builds upon ongoing One Health-related work. It is designed to operate at both national and subnational levels, with specific timeframes for implementation. The plan must also align with the global Quadripartite OH JPA framework. Sharing lessons learned is a critical cross-cutting activity. This involves disseminating outcomes, outputs, and insights from national One Health implementation efforts to other stakeholders. The first stage of implementation involves conducting a situation analysis. This includes mapping and analyzing stakeholders at the national level, reviewing governance and coordination mechanisms for One Health, and identifying strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT). Additionally, it involves reviewing completed national assessments related to One Health, identifying gaps, and planning future assessments if necessary. If no recent assessments have been conducted, a new One Health assessment should be carried out using existing tools. Existing national action plans, strategies, frameworks, and activities related to One Health should be identified and described. This includes evaluating their alignment with the six action tracks of the OH JPA and identifying any gaps. The second stage focuses on establishing or strengthening a multisectoral One Health coordination mechanism. This mechanism should include details on its establishment, the sectors represented, and its governance structure, which should reflect a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach. Gender equity must be integrated into the mechanism, ensuring gender sensitivity in all aspects of governance. For countries without such a mechanism, it is essential to establish one before proceeding to the next stage of planning. The third stage involves planning for implementation. This includes prioritizing activities based on the action tracks and pathways of change outlined in the OH JPA, tailored to the country’s specific needs and context. The findings from the situation analysis in Stage 1 should guide this prioritization. Strategic objectives and outcomes for the national One Health action plan should be clearly defined, and a detailed workplan and budget should be developed. Monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) frameworks should also be established to track progress. Resource mobilization is a key component of the plan, focusing on securing sustainable funding and institutionalizing the One Health approach. This includes exploring domestic and international financing options, as well as conducting economic analyses or investment planning to demonstrate the return on investment for One Health interventions. Contact information for the focal points or offices responsible for implementing and monitoring the national One Health action plan should be provided. Additionally, relevant references, such as existing national action plans and assessment reports, should be listed. Annex 2 provides a link to the One Health High-Level Expert Panel (OHHLEP) inventory of tools and resources. These resources can assist countries in identifying tools for capacity assessment and operationalizing One Health. They can also help identify completed One Health-related assessments to inform national priorities and establish or strengthen One Health mechanisms.
